sections.title: DECISION GUIDE: "Which Technique Should I Use?"
sections.body:
### How to Choose: Regression vs Classification?
```
Is your target variable CONTINUOUS (numbers like price, salary)?
  → REGRESSION

Is your target variable CATEGORICAL (categories like yes/no, spam/not-spam)?
  → CLASSIFICATION
```

### How to Handle Missing Values?
```
Missing Values Decision:
│
├── Numerical Column:
│   ├── Normal Distribution → Use MEAN
│   ├── Skewed Distribution → Use MEDIAN  ← (MOST COMMON, SAFEST)
│   └── Too many missing (>50%) → DROP the column
│
├── Categorical Column:
│   ├── Few missing → Use MODE (most frequent value)
│   └── Too many missing (>50%) → DROP the column
│
└── Advanced:
    ├── KNN Imputer → Uses nearby data points
    └── Iterative Imputer → Uses other features to predict
```

### How to Encode Categorical Variables?
```
Encoding Decision:
│
├── Only 2 categories (Yes/No, Male/Female):
│   └── Label Encoding (0, 1)
│
├── Multiple categories WITH order (Low/Medium/High):
│   └── Ordinal Encoding (0, 1, 2)
│
├── Multiple categories WITHOUT order (Red/Blue/Green):
│   ├── Few categories (<10) → One-Hot Encoding  ← MOST COMMON
│   └── Many categories (>10) → Target Encoding
│
└── Tree-based models (Random Forest, XGBoost):
    └── Label Encoding works fine (trees can handle it)
```

### How to Scale Features?
```
Scaling Decision:
│
├── StandardScaler (z-score normalization):
│   └── Use when: Data is normally distributed
│   └── Best for: Linear Regression, Logistic Regression, SVM, KNN
│
├── MinMaxScaler (0 to 1 range):
│   └── Use when: You want values between 0 and 1
│   └── Best for: Neural Networks, KNN
│
├── RobustScaler:
│   └── Use when: Data has OUTLIERS
│   └── Uses median and IQR instead of mean and std
│
└── Tree-based models (Random Forest, XGBoost):
    └── DON'T NEED SCALING! Trees split on values, scale doesn't matter
```

### How to Handle Outliers?
```
Outlier Decision:
│
├── Detect:
│   ├── IQR Method → Q1 - 1.5*IQR to Q3 + 1.5*IQR (MOST COMMON)
│   ├── Z-score → Values beyond 3 standard deviations
│   └── Visualization → Box plots
│
├── Handle:
│   ├── Remove → If outliers are errors/noise
│   ├── Cap/Clip → Replace with upper/lower bounds (SAFEST)
│   ├── Transform → Log transformation, Square root
│   └── Keep → If outliers are genuine (e.g., CEO salary)
│
└── Tree-based models:
    └── Generally ROBUST to outliers (less worry needed)
```

### How to Choose the Model?
```
REGRESSION Models (predicting numbers):
│
├── Start Simple: Linear Regression
├── If overfitting: Ridge or Lasso Regression
├── Non-linear patterns: Decision Tree Regressor
├── Better accuracy: Random Forest Regressor  ← USUALLY BEST
├── Even better: Gradient Boosting / XGBoost  ← TOP PERFORMER
└── Always try: Multiple models and compare!

CLASSIFICATION Models (predicting categories):
│
├── Start Simple: Logistic Regression
├── Distance-based: KNN (K-Nearest Neighbors)
├── Rule-based: Decision Tree Classifier
├── Better accuracy: Random Forest Classifier  ← USUALLY BEST
├── Best accuracy: Gradient Boosting / XGBoost  ← TOP PERFORMER
├── Works well with scaling: SVM
└── Always try: Multiple models and compare!
```

### How to Evaluate Models?

```
REGRESSION Metrics:
│
├── MAE (Mean Absolute Error) → Average mistake size
├── MSE (Mean Squared Error) → Penalizes big mistakes more
├── RMSE (Root MSE) → Same unit as target (MOST USED)
├── R² Score → How much variance explained (1.0 = perfect)
└── Adjusted R² → R² adjusted for number of features

CLASSIFICATION Metrics:
│
├── Accuracy → % correct predictions (DON'T use if imbalanced!)
├── Precision → Of predicted positives, how many correct?
├── Recall → Of actual positives, how many found?
├── F1-Score → Balance between Precision & Recall (MOST USED)
├── ROC-AUC → Overall classification ability
└── Confusion Matrix → Visual breakdown of predictions
```
